title: Claude solves 25-year NSA cryptography mystery
dek: Anthropic’s Claude identified the source of NIST curve seeds in under 30 minutes, reducing concerns about a deliberate backdoor.
body:
Anthropic’s AI model Claude figured out the origin of a 25-year-old mystery about the seeds used to generate NIST standard elliptic-curve parameters for digital signatures. The seeds were published by the NSA without explanation when the curves were adopted, prompting long-standing suspicion that the agency might have inserted a backdoor. Claude determined in under 30 minutes that the seeds were produced by lrand48, a simple pseudorandom number generator used in C libraries, which makes a deliberate, sophisticated backdoor less likely.

## Why it matters

The choice of initial seeds for cryptographic curves matters because if those seeds were chosen to hide special structure, an attacker could potentially forge digital signatures or break keys. The NSA’s lack of explanation for how the seeds were generated fed decades of distrust among cryptographers and security practitioners. If the seeds can be traced to a known, simple RNG, the chance that the published parameters contain an intentional, hidden weakness decreases — shifting the conversation from suspicion of malice to questions about transparency and good practice.

## The details

- The problem: NIST adopted elliptic-curve parameters for digital signatures whose published seeds lacked a documented source, creating a long-running question about whether the curves contained a hidden vulnerability.  
- The investigator: Claude is an AI model developed by Anthropic.  
- The finding: Claude identified that the seeds match outputs of lrand48, a simple C library pseudorandom number generator (PRNG).  
- Timing: Anthropic reports that Claude reached this result in under 30 minutes.  
- Implication: Because lrand48 is a known, straightforward PRNG, this finding makes a deliberate, sophisticated backdoor in the published curves less likely.  
- Remaining gaps: Public reporting does not say whether independent cryptographers have reproduced Claude’s work, nor whether additional analysis of the curves has changed as a result.

## What to watch

Independent verification by human cryptographers and independent teams will be crucial; the broader community typically requires reproducible, peer-reviewed analysis before changing trust decisions. Expect follow-up scrutiny of both the curves and the method Claude used to reach the result, since adoption or continued use of cryptographic standards rests on community validation and transparent provenance.

Source: [The Decoder](https://the-decoder.com/anthropics-claude-cracks-a-25-year-old-nsa-cryptography-mystery-in-under-30-minutes/)
